title: Web Export: TARGET_NOT_SUPPORTED crash in Android Facebook in-app browser
body:
### Tested versions

-4.6 stabil 

### System information

Android 16 - Samsung S23 Ultra - Godot 4.6 stabil

### Issue description

OS: Android (Tested on Android 16)
Browser: Android Facebook In-App Browser (WebView / Chrome 146)

### Issue description
When trying to run a Godot 4 Web Export inside the Android Facebook App's built-in browser, the game crashes at loading. 

The console throws the following Emscripten-generated error at line 1 in `index.js`:
`TARGET_NOT_SUPPORTED;if(currentSafariVersion<150200){throw new Error("This emscripten-generated code requires Safari v15.2.0 or newer...")}`

**The underlying issue:**
The Android Facebook In-App Browser has a very messy User-Agent string that includes both Chrome and Mobile Safari, along with Facebook's custom tags. 
Example User-Agent
Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 16; SM-S918B Build/BP2A.250605.031.A3; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/146.0.7680.168 Mobile Safari/537.36 [FB_IAB/FB4A;FBAV/554.0.0.57.70;IABMV/1;]

Because of this UA string, Emscripten's browser detection gets confused. It detects the word "Safari", fails to parse the correct version due to the Facebook tags, assumes it's an outdated Safari version, and throws a fatal exception. 

**The Proof / Workaround:**
The underlying Chromium WebView actually fully supports all required modern features (like Wasm exception handling). **If I manually open the exported `index.js` and delete the `if(currentSafariVersion<150200){...}` check, the game runs perfectly and flawlessly inside the Android Facebook browser!** *(Note: The game also runs perfectly in the iOS Facebook in-app browser out of the box, as the iOS WebKit User-Agent is parsed correctly by Emscripten. The issue is strictly isolated to Android's FB browser UA).*

This means we are losing a massive amount of Android mobile players simply due to a false positive browser detection regex in the Emscripten glue code.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Export any Godot 4.6-stable project to Web.
2. Host it on a server.
3. Post it on Facebook.
4. Open the link on an Android device using the Facebook App.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - This applies to any blank Godot 4 web export.
